title: Positivist Calendar
intro: Auguste Comte's proposed Positivist calendar reorganises the year into equal months named for historical figures.
structure: Thirteen months each have 28 days, or four seven-day weeks; additional festival days bring the year to 365 or 366 days. These are separate from regular month days.
model: The provider uses Gregorian year alignment and leap rules with Great Crisis year numbering equal to Gregorian year minus 1788.
example: Gregorian 2026 corresponds to Great Crisis Year 238. Each standard month has four complete weeks.
history: Comte devised the calendar in the nineteenth century as a social and intellectual reform. Month names reflect figures he regarded as important to humanity's development.
limits: The proposal was not general historical civil practice; retrospective mathematical projections do not establish adoption.
